canonical.title: Number of Ways to Arrive at Destination in Shortest Time
canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/4. Shortest Path Problems/11. Number of ways to arrive the destination with minimum distance.cpp

narrative.title: Counting the Fastest Response Corridors
narrative.scenario: An emergency network plans dispatch routes between junctions, and the controller wants to know how many distinct fastest corridors exist from base to the incident site — every one of them must be pre-cleared. Whenever two routes tie on total minutes, they count separately; the tally can be huge, so it is reported modulo 10^9 + 7.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n (junctions 0..n-1) and a list roads where [u, v, t] is a bidirectional road taking t minutes.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the number of distinct shortest-time routes from 0 to n-1, modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: At most one road between any two junctions; the graph is connected

testCases.explanation: The direct 2-minute road and the 1+1 chain tie — two fastest routes.
A single corridor offers exactly one way to arrive.

hintLevels: Level 1: Dijkstra finds the fastest time; a second number rides along counting how you got there.
Level 2: Strictly faster arrival replaces the count; an equal arrival adds the predecessor's count.
Level 3: Take the count modulo at every addition, and prefer 64-bit sums for the time values.
